answer_sql:
WITH by_channel AS (
  SELECT
    channel,
    SUM(net_amount) AS net_sales
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  WHERE
    channel IN ('online', 'physical')
  GROUP BY
    channel
)
SELECT
  channel,
  net_sales AS sales_usd_net,
  MAX(CASE WHEN channel = 'online' THEN net_sales END) OVER () / MAX(CASE WHEN channel = 'physical' THEN net_sales END) OVER () AS sales_ratio_internet_to_physical
FROM by_channel
ORDER BY
  channel

body.value: Two rows as returned, one per selling channel. Each says how much money that channel took from customers after discount, in USD, across every sale on record over the full ten years 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31: 86,790,054.13 for the web shop, 132,024,417.53 for the walk-in shops. Beside both sits one figure describing the two together, 0.657379 — the web shop's ten-year takings divided by the walk-in shops' — meaning the internet business took about 66 cents for every dollar the physical shops took. It repeats on both rows because it is a property of the pair, not of either row. WHAT THESE FIGURES DO NOT INCLUDE: no period restriction, so this is all ten years and not a year or a month; no currency conversion, because the amounts are already USD whatever currency the sale was transacted in; no deduction for returns or tax, neither of which this bundle records, so "net" means net of DISCOUNT only; and no trading-state restriction, so sales rung up at the 16 premises that have since closed are counted inside the physical total. The two channels are exhaustive, accounting for all 223,974 lines and all 93,470 orders and summing to 218,814,471.66 USD, so no other channel's revenue sits outside this comparison.

    SUM(gross_amount) AS gross_sales
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  WHERE
    channel IN ('online', 'physical')
  GROUP BY
    channel
), pair AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN channel = 'online' THEN net_sales END) AS online_net,
    MAX(CASE WHEN channel = 'physical' THEN net_sales END) AS physical_net,
    SUM(net_sales) AS total_net,
    MAX(CASE WHEN channel = 'online' THEN gross_sales END) AS online_gross,
    MAX(CASE WHEN channel = 'physical' THEN gross_sales END) AS physical_gross
  FROM by_channel
)
SELECT
  b.channel,
  b.net_sales,
  p.online_net / p.physical_net AS ratio_internet_to_physical,
  p.online_net / p.total_net AS alt_internet_share_of_total,
  p.physical_net / p.online_net AS alt_physical_to_internet,
  p.online_gross / p.physical_gross AS alt_ratio_on_gross
FROM by_channel AS b
CROSS JOIN pair AS p
ORDER BY
  b.channel

value.sql:
WITH by_channel AS (
  SELECT
    channel,
    SUM(net_amount) AS net_sales
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  WHERE
    channel IN ('online', 'physical')
  GROUP BY
    channel
)
SELECT
  channel,
  net_sales AS sales_usd_net,
  MAX(CASE WHEN channel = 'online' THEN net_sales END) OVER () / MAX(CASE WHEN channel = 'physical' THEN net_sales END) OVER () AS sales_ratio_internet_to_physical
FROM by_channel
ORDER BY
  channel
value.means: Two rows as returned, one per selling channel. Each says how much money that channel took from customers after discount, in USD, across every sale on record over the full ten years 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31: 86,790,054.13 for the web shop, 132,024,417.53 for the walk-in shops. Beside both sits one figure describing the two together, 0.657379 — the web shop's ten-year takings divided by the walk-in shops' — meaning the internet business took about 66 cents for every dollar the physical shops took. It repeats on both rows because it is a property of the pair, not of either row. WHAT THESE FIGURES DO NOT INCLUDE: no period restriction, so this is all ten years and not a year or a month; no currency conversion, because the amounts are already USD whatever currency the sale was transacted in; no deduction for returns or tax, neither of which this bundle records, so "net" means net of DISCOUNT only; and no trading-state restriction, so sales rung up at the 16 premises that have since closed are counted inside the physical total. The two channels are exhaustive, accounting for all 223,974 lines and all 93,470 orders and summing to 218,814,471.66 USD, so no other channel's revenue sits outside this comparison.

readings.could_also_mean: internet as a share of all sales = 0.396638 (39.7%), a materially different figure and the one a reader asking "how much of our business is online" would want; or physical divided by internet = 1.521193. I did not ask because the question names the denominator itself — step 5 orders its inputs internet-then-physical and output_shape labels the column "sales ratio (internet to physical)". All three are measured from the same two totals and stated here, so a reader who meant another can point at it without further work.
